biometransitions.config.advanced.climate:
0 = same mixing distance everywhere; 1 = very different climates get a much narrower zone.
Example: at 0.3 a desert/snow transition is about 22%% narrower than a forest/forest one.
biometransitions.config.advanced.fluidTr: Mix water features (seagrass, kelp...) in a separate, narrower zone.
biometransitions.config.advanced.maxNeig: How many different neighbouring biomes one spot can mix in.
biometransitions.config.advanced.prevent:
Extra check that a mixed-in feature does not land directly on another feature's blocks (a rock on a rock, a plant on leaves).
Touching and overlapping crowns stay allowed. Off = no extra checks.
biometransitions.config.advanced.undergr: Also look for boundaries of underground biomes.
biometransitions.config.classification.g:
Group names offered for biomes in the list below, comma separated.
Example: forest, snowy, desert, ocean, my_group
biometransitions.config.classification.o: Biome id -> groups. Replaces the tag rules for that biome.
biometransitions.config.classification.t: Rules {tags: [...], categories: [...]}: a biome with all the tags gets the groups.
biometransitions.config.colors.reducedBi: Biomes that use the shorter Reduced Distance below (e.g. swamps, so their dark water stays crisp).
biometransitions.config.colors.reducedDi: Colour blending distance for Reduced Biomes.
biometransitions.config.colors.sameAsMix:
On: colours blend as far as features mix (Mixing Distance), capped by Max Biome Color Blending.
Off: colours always use Max Biome Color Blending.
biometransitions.config.debug.collectSta: Count placements and rejections for /btg stats.
biometransitions.config.debug.extremePre:
Testing only: biomes generate no features of their own outside transitions,
so the transition zones stand out clearly. Never use in a real world.
biometransitions.config.debug.logRejecti: Write every rejected placement to the log (very verbose).
biometransitions.config.density.other.to: Density mode for everything else: rocks, ground patches, terrain decorations...
biometransitions.config.density.treesAnd: Density mode for trees, bushes, grass, flowers and other plants.
biometransitions.config.distribution.cur:
Shape of the transition: how the neighbour's share of the features falls with the distance from the boundary.
One curve spans the whole transition, from the zone edge in one biome across the boundary to the zone edge
in the other, so both sides always agree: 50/50 at the boundary when both biomes spread into each other,
100%% neighbour at the boundary when only the neighbour spreads (A into B pairs).
The curve never changes how far the zone reaches; that is Mixing Distance.
biometransitions.config.distribution.cus:
Points of the CUSTOM curve, evenly spaced from the zone edge (first) to the boundary (last), 0..1.
The last point counts as the balanced mix at the boundary; the other side of the boundary mirrors the curve.
Example: 0, 0.1, 0.35, 0.75, 1 = the neighbour stays rare in the outer half and grows quickly near the boundary.
biometransitions.config.distribution.fal:
Exponent on the distance inside each biome. 1 = the curve as chosen.
Below 1 the neighbour reaches further at high strength; above 1 it fades sooner.
Example: 2 = at half the distance the neighbour has about half the share it has at 1.
biometransitions.config.distribution.int:
Overall strength of the mix. 1 = 50/50 at the boundary.
Below 1 each biome keeps more of its own features (less mixing on both sides);
above 1 the neighbour dominates on both sides near the boundary.
Example: 0.5 = at most 25%% neighbour features at the boundary.
biometransitions.config.distribution.nei:
Weight of the neighbour's features. Higher = the neighbour comes in more.
Example: own 1, neighbour 3 = 75%% neighbour features at the boundary instead of 50%%.
biometransitions.config.distribution.noi:
How much large-scale noise bends the transition, so the balanced 50/50 line wanders instead of following
the biome boundary exactly. 0 = straight. The NOISE curve doubles this.
The zone edges stay at the configured distance.
Size of the noise waves. Small = ragged, large = long gentle waves.
biometransitions.config.distribution.own:
Weight of the biome's own features. Higher = the neighbour comes in less.
Example: own 3, neighbour 1 = 25%% neighbour features at the boundary instead of 50%%.
biometransitions.config.distribution.ran:
Per-column randomness of the mix inside the transition. 0 = perfectly regular.
Never moves the zone edges, so features never reach further than the configured distance.
biometransitions.config.distribution.sha: How the distance to the boundary is measured.
biometransitions.config.distribution.smo:
Pull the curve towards a smooth S shape. 0 = curve as chosen, 1 = fully smoothed.
Useful to soften the sharp corners of CUSTOM curves.
biometransitions.config.distribution.sup:
Thin out the biome's own features as the neighbour's come in, so the mix really shifts from A to B.
Off = the neighbour's features are only added on top.
Ground of group A (e.g. sand) can appear in group B; B's ground stays out of A.
Ground of group B can appear in group A; A's ground stays out of B.
Ground of both biomes spreads into the opposite biome.
Surface blocks are not mixed between the two groups.
biometransitions.config.enum.curve.custo: Your own shape from the Custom Curve points.
biometransitions.config.enum.curve.ease_: The neighbour's share drops quickly near the boundary, then thins out slowly towards the zone edge.
A steeper S curve over the whole transition: a sharp change at the boundary, long soft tails.
The neighbour stays strong for a long way from the boundary, then fades quickly near the zone edge.
biometransitions.config.enum.curve.linea: The neighbour's share falls at a constant rate from the boundary to the zone edge.
biometransitions.config.enum.curve.logar:
The neighbour's share drops very fast right next to the boundary, then decreases ever more slowly,
leaving a long thin tail of rare neighbour features up to the zone edge.
Example: at half the distance roughly 10%% neighbour features are left (LINEAR: about 25%%).
biometransitions.config.enum.curve.noise: Like LINEAR, with twice the Noise Influence for a strongly irregular transition.
biometransitions.config.enum.curve.smoot:
One S curve over the whole transition: the mix changes fastest at the boundary and eases out softly
towards both zone edges.
biometransitions.config.enum.densitymode:
The whole transition gets the average density of both biomes.
Example: forest 100 trees, plains 40 trees -> 70 trees everywhere in the zone.

Density changes smoothly with the distance from the boundary.
Example: 100 trees deep in the forest, falling to 40 towards the plains.
How the feature count in a transition is decided.
biometransitions.config.enum.intersectio: Where three or more biomes meet (two or more neighbours reach a spot), nothing is mixed.
Every neighbour mixes in by its own Biome Boundary Mixing rules.
biometransitions.config.enum.layer.surfa: Only at the surface, not in caves.
biometransitions.config.enum.layer.under: Only underground (more than 6 blocks below the surface).
biometransitions.config.enum.mixmode.a_i: Features of group A spread into group B; B stays out of A.
biometransitions.config.enum.mixmode.b_i: Features of group B spread into group A; A stays out of B.
biometransitions.config.enum.mixmode.bot: Both groups spread their features into each other.
biometransitions.config.enum.mixmode.do_: The two groups never mix their features.
biometransitions.config.enum.replacemode: By the Custom Mapping, e.g. ocean-river turns small oceans into the nearest river.
Nearest biome of the same group (a small birch forest becomes the surrounding forest).
Nearest biome with the most similar climate (temperature and rainfall).
biometransitions.config.enum.shape.diamo: Manhattan distance: zones are narrower diagonally.
biometransitions.config.enum.shape.round: Circular distance: zones follow the boundary smoothly.
biometransitions.config.enum.shape.squar: Chessboard distance: zones are wider diagonally.
biometransitions.config.enum.varietybala: No balancing: a biome with many kinds of features shows all of them at full rate.
A neighbour with more kinds of features than this biome has each kind thinned, so it cannot dominate the mix.
Balance only trees and foliage; rocks and other features keep full rate.
biometransitions.config.featurerules.ena: Decoration steps whose features may be mixed.
biometransitions.config.featurerules.exc: Feature types never mixed, never thinned and never suppressed: ores, structures and order-dependent features.
biometransitions.config.featurerules.key: Keyword in the placed feature id -> category, first match wins.
Biomes the feature may be mixed into (ids, tags, group names). Empty = any.

Block ids or #tags allowed directly below the feature. Empty = any.
Example: #minecraft:dirt = only on grass, dirt, podzol...
Allow features to be mixed at all.
Density multiplier per feature (on top of the category and global multipliers).
Where the feature may be placed.
Placement positions tried per feature and chunk.
Largest height difference to the neighbouring columns. 16 = no limit.
0 = off; otherwise each placement must be within this distance of an earlier one (clusters).
Highest Y the feature may be placed at.
Minimum distance between two placements of the same feature (within a chunk). 0 = off.
Lowest Y the feature may be placed at.
Free blocks required above the spot (e.g. 4 for trees).
Chance to win a spot several features compete for. 0.01 = almost never, 10 = almost always.
biometransitions.config.fluid.allowFluid: Allow lakes and springs to be carried over. Off = no new water bodies.
biometransitions.config.fluid.allowLandF: Allow land features to be placed in water.
biometransitions.config.fluid.allowedFlu: Fluid ids or #tags that water features may use.
Density multiplier of mixed-in water features.
biometransitions.config.fluid.shoreFrequ: Density multiplier for shore plants next to water.
biometransitions.config.fluid.shoreRadiu: Shore plants within this distance of water get the shore frequency.
biometransitions.config.fluid.width.tool: Width of the water feature zone.
biometransitions.config.general.biomeRep: Replace too small biome areas (see Biome Replacing), e.g. tiny oceans in the middle of a river system.
biometransitions.config.general.colorBle:
Largest distance over which grass, foliage and water colours blend between biomes (client side).
0 = vanilla colour blending (Options → Video Settings → Biome Blend).
Example: 32 = the grass colour changes gradually over about 64 blocks across a boundary.
Same value as in Biome Color Blending.
biometransitions.config.general.dimensio: Dimension ids where the mod generates transitions, e.g. minecraft:overworld. Empty = all dimensions.
Master switch. Off = the mod does nothing in newly generated chunks
(colour blending falls back to vanilla as well).
biometransitions.config.general.mixSurfa:
Allow surface biomes and underground (cave) biomes to mix their features.
Off = lush caves and the forest above them stay separate.
biometransitions.config.general.mixingDi:
How far features of a neighbouring biome reach into a biome, measured from the boundary.
0 = no feature mixing, 128 = very wide, soft transitions.
Example: 64 = forest trees still appear (rarely) 64 blocks deep into the plains.
The same setting is shown in General and in Biome Mixing; both edit one value.
Tree Mixing Distance, Block Blending Distance and pairs in Biome Boundary Mixing can override it.
biometransitions.config.general.surfaceM:
Spread the neighbour's ground (sand, grass, snow...) into the transition in natural patches,
so its plants have something to grow on. Details in Biome Mixing → Surface block blending.
Biomes that act as a wall: features do not mix between biomes on opposite sides of them.
Example: river = forest trees do not jump over a river into the plains.
biometransitions.config.mixing.blendOnly:
Biomes that blend only with their own group. Join groups with + to make one group:
desert+badlands = desert and badlands blend with each other, but with nothing else.
biometransitions.config.mixing.intersect: What happens where three or more biomes meet.
biometransitions.config.mixing.noBlend.t:
Biomes that do not blend with anything: no features, no surface blocks and no snow cross their boundary,
in either direction. Wins over every pair in Biome Boundary Mixing.
Accepts biome ids (minecraft:river), tags (#minecraft:is_ocean) and group names (ocean).
biometransitions.config.mixing.noSurface: Biomes whose ground never spreads and never receives foreign ground (or snow). Their features still mix.
biometransitions.config.mixing.similarDi:
Mixing distance multiplier for biomes of a similar group (both forests, both taigas...).
1 = same as other pairs, 2 = twice as wide.
Applies to the global Mixing, Tree and Block Blending distances, not to pairs with their own distance.
biometransitions.config.mixing.treeMixin:
How far trees of a neighbouring biome reach into a biome, separately from the other features.
Left end = same as Mixing Distance. Rocks, plants and other vegetation keep using Mixing Distance.
Example: Mixing Distance 48 and Tree Mixing Distance 96 = flowers and grass mix over 48 blocks,
while single trees of the neighbour still appear up to 96 blocks deep.
Pairs in Biome Boundary Mixing can override it with their own Tree Mixing Distance.
biometransitions.config.mixing.varietyBa:
Keeps a biome with many kinds of features from flooding the transition with them.
Example: a jungle (many plants) next to plains (few) has each jungle plant thinned.
biometransitions.config.pairrule.a.toolt: Group A: biome id (minecraft:forest), tag (#minecraft:is_forest) or group name (forest).
biometransitions.config.pairrule.b.toolt: Group B: biome id (minecraft:plains), tag (#c:is_plains) or group name (plains).
biometransitions.config.pairrule.blockDi:
Which direction surface blocks (sand, grass, snow...) spread in, independently of the Feature Direction.
Example: desert + jungle with Feature Direction BOTH and Block Blending A into B = sand spreads into the jungle,
jungle grass never appears in the desert, while plants of both still mix.
Needs Surface Mixing on in General; No Blend and No Surface Blend lists always win.

How far surface blocks of the other biome may appear from the boundary for this pair.
Left end (-1) = this pair's Mixing Distance. Example: Mixing Distance 80 and -1 here = sand patches reach 80 blocks.
Right end (129) = Global: Block Blending Distance from Boundary in Biome Mixing.
biometransitions.config.pairrule.curve.t: Mixing distribution curve for this pair (features and surface blocks). Global = setting from Biome Mixing.
biometransitions.config.pairrule.distanc:
How far features reach across the boundary for this pair.
Global = Mixing Distance from General (times the similar-group multiplier).
biometransitions.config.pairrule.mode.to: Which direction features (trees, plants, rocks...) spread in. Surface blocks have their own direction below.
biometransitions.config.pairrule.otherDe: Density mode for other features. Global = setting from Biome Mixing.
biometransitions.config.pairrule.treeDis:
How far trees reach across the boundary for this pair.
Left end (-1) = this pair's Mixing Distance. Example: Mixing Distance 80 and -1 here = trees mix over 80 blocks.
Right end (129) = Global: Tree Mixing Distance from Biome Mixing (when that is "= Mixing Distance", this pair's Mixing Distance).
biometransitions.config.pairrule.treesAn: Density mode for trees and foliage. Global = setting from Biome Mixing.
biometransitions.config.pairrule.variety: Feature variety balancing. Global = setting from Biome Mixing.
biometransitions.config.performance.cach: Boundary results kept in memory. More = less recomputation, more RAM.
biometransitions.config.performance.maxC: Upper limit of mixed-in feature candidates per chunk and step.
biometransitions.config.performance.maxP: Upper limit of mixed-in features actually placed per chunk and step.
biometransitions.config.performance.unde: Check every n-th 16-block section below the surface for underground boundaries. 1 = every section (slowest).
biometransitions.config.replacing.change: What a small biome turns into.
biometransitions.config.replacing.custom:
Custom replacement pairs, source-target, separated by commas: ocean-river,forest-plains.
The nearest biome matching the target (also further away) is used; if none is found, nothing is replaced.
biometransitions.config.replacing.neverR: Biomes that are never replaced. Highest priority: wins over Small Biomes with Biome ID Replacement.
biometransitions.config.replacing.overla:
Used by Overlapping Detection of small biomes: a biome counts as small when the mixing zones of its neighbours
(Mixing Distance x this value) cover all of it.
1.0 = full mixing distance; lower = only very narrow biomes count as small.
Example: Mixing Distance 64 and 0.4 = areas no more than about 25 blocks from their edge anywhere are small.
Does not change how far features mix.
biometransitions.config.replacing.replac:
Small Biomes with Biome ID Replacement: biomes whose small areas are replaced by another biome
(biome ids, tags, group names). Example: ocean = tiny ocean pools become river.

Areas smaller than this (in quarts = 4x4 blocks) are replaced. 306 quarts = about 70 x 70 blocks.
-1 = Overlapping Detection: small = fully covered by the neighbours' mixing zones.
biometransitions.config.replacing.smallB:
Measure the size of biome areas in quarts (4x4 block biome cells, the resolution Minecraft samples biomes at).
Needed by everything in this section: off = no biome is ever replaced and no feature is suppressed.
biometransitions.config.replacing.suppre:
Small Biomes with Feature Suppression: biomes that keep their id when small, but generate none of their own features.
The surrounding biomes' features grow there instead (by the mixing rules), and the small area
spreads none of its features into its neighbours. Features the surrounding biomes have as well
(ores, common grass...) and excluded feature types keep generating, so no holes appear.
Example: minecraft:birch_forest = small birch patches inside a forest grow oak forest instead.
Areas smaller than this (in quarts) lose their own features. -1 = Overlapping Detection.
biometransitions.config.selection.allowe: Feature categories that may be mixed.
biometransitions.config.selection.catego: Density multiplier per feature category, e.g. {"trees": 0.5}. Missing = 1.
biometransitions.config.selection.exclud: Placed feature ids that are never mixed.
biometransitions.config.selection.freque: Density multiplier of mixed-in features. Above 1 the zone can be denser than the source biome.
biometransitions.config.surface.blockBle:
How far from a biome boundary surface blocks (and snow) of the neighbouring biome may appear,
independently of how far features mix. Left end = same as the feature Mixing Distance.
Example: Mixing Distance 64 and 16 here = trees mix over 64 blocks, sand patches stay within 16 blocks.
Pairs in Biome Boundary Mixing can override it.
biometransitions.config.surface.blocks.t: Biome or group -> [top block, block below]. First match of the neighbour wins; biomes without an entry spread no ground.
biometransitions.config.surface.depth.to: How many blocks deep the ground is replaced.
biometransitions.config.surface.intensit: How much of the zone gets the neighbour's ground. 0 = none, 1 = about the neighbour's share, 2 = most of it.
biometransitions.config.surface.patchSca: Size of the ground patches. Small = many small spots, large = big blobs.
biometransitions.config.surface.replacea: Only these blocks are ever replaced (ids or #tags), so stone, ores and structures stay untouched.
biometransitions.config.surface.snowLaye:
Carry snow layers of cold neighbours into the transition, in the same patches as their ground.
Snow is only placed where the neighbour would snow itself (cold enough at that height, open sky,
a solid or leafy block below, never on ice or water).
biometransitions.gui.groups.tooltip:
Groups of %s: %s

Click = next group, right click = previous group, mouse wheel = scroll through the groups.
Auto = the groups the tag rules give this biome.
Options are the names from Biome Groups above.
biometransitions.gui.note.biomes.menu: Vanilla biomes only: open the config from inside a world (Esc → Mods) to see modded biomes and their automatic groups.
biometransitions.gui.note.biomes.world: All biomes of this world, modded ones included. Auto = groups from the tag rules above; picking a group replaces them for that biome.
biometransitions.gui.note.classification: Every biome belongs to one or more groups (forest, snowy, desert...). Groups are what the mixing rules, pairs and lists refer to. Special selectors that need no assignment: all, surface, underground.
biometransitions.gui.note.colors: Grass, foliage and water colours blend smoothly across biome boundaries. Client side only; changes apply to the visible world immediately after Save.
biometransitions.gui.note.density: How many features the transition gets in total. Where they come from is decided by Distribution below.
biometransitions.gui.note.distances: How far a neighbour's features reach into a biome. Mixing Distance is the same setting as in General: changing it here changes it there.
biometransitions.gui.note.distribution.c: One curve runs across the whole transition, from the zone edge in one biome over the boundary to the zone edge in the other, and both biomes use it. Pairs mixing both ways meet 50/50 at the boundary; one-way pairs (A into B) start at 100%% of A right at the boundary and fade out inside B.
biometransitions.gui.note.distribution.s: Curve and Falloff shape how the neighbour fades, Intensity and the two Influences set how strong it is, Noise and Random Variation make it irregular. None of them moves the zone edge: that is the Mixing Distance.
biometransitions.gui.note.distribution.w: Distribution decides which biome's features appear where inside the transition: the neighbour's share of the features at every distance from the boundary.
biometransitions.gui.note.groups: Type the group names you want to use, separated by commas. Every name listed here can be assigned to biomes below.
biometransitions.gui.note.hover: Hover any setting for an explanation, an example and its default value.
biometransitions.gui.note.mixing_rules: Which biomes may mix at all. These lists win over every pair in Biome Boundary Mixing.
biometransitions.gui.note.pairs: Pairs not listed here mix by the global Biome Mixing settings. First matching pair wins. Features and surface blocks have separate directions and distances; click a pair to see them.
biometransitions.gui.note.small_biome_de: Measures biome areas, so too small ones can be replaced or lose their own features (formerly Boundary Detection).
biometransitions.gui.note.surface_blendi: The neighbour's ground (sand, grass...) and snow spread into the transition in patches, so its plants can grow. Turned on and off with Surface Mixing in General; pairs set their own direction and distance.
biometransitions.gui.note.surface_compat: Rules every mixed-in feature must meet; per category and per feature overrides are in JSON.
biometransitions.gui.pair.reset_all.tool: Replace the whole list with the default pairs (%s realistic neighbours).
biometransitions.gui.search.tooltip: Filter the biome list by name (Dark Forest) or id (minecraft:dark_forest) while you type.
biometransitions.gui.slider.exact: Type an exact value in the box.
biometransitions.gui.title: Biome Transition Generator
